chunks: Ali, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'adah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Do not employ foolish wet-nurses, for the milk overcomes the natures.' And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not employ foolish wet-nurses, for the child grows upon it.'

key_terms.اللَّبَنَ: Milk (specifically breast milk in this context)
key_terms.يَشِبُّ عَلَيْهِ: Grows upon it / is influenced by it

ai.seo_question: Why should one avoid employing foolish wet-nurses according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, found in al-Kafi’s chapter on wet-nursing, highlights the Shia belief in the physiological and spiritual transmission of character traits through milk, a concept known as 'radāʿ'. Imam Ali and the Prophet Muhammad both warn against selecting 'al-ḥamqāʾ' (the foolish or lacking prudence) as wet-nurses, asserting that milk dominates natural disposition and that the child inherits the nurse's qualities. This underscores the importance of choosing a nurse with both sound intellect and piety to ensure the child's moral and intellectual development.
